transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-10 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 54 minutes (approx)
- Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Nia O'Connor (Redwood Solutions); Lena Ortiz, Marcus Feng, Sana Rahman, Tom Brewer (Pioneer Biomed)

Auto-generated summary (optional):
- High-level posture review for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 readiness. Discussed where Pioneer will need evidence exports, Trust Center read access, RBAC for auditor roles, KMS/encryption flows and data residency constraints for EU patients. Agreed next steps: share redacted reports, provide controls mapping template, schedule Dedicated VPC walkthrough.

Topics covered:
- Scope and current posture (what controls already in place)
- Trust Center access model and roles for auditors
- Audit log retention, SIEM integrations, and export formats
- KMS flow and envelope encryption for PHI/PII data
- Data residency needs (EU vs US) and private deployment options
- Evidence handoff process and timelines for Pioneer audit window

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into posture and evidence flow.
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: Hey Ava, hi Samir — Lena here. We're on a pretty tight timeline, our external audit window is mid-December, so we wanted to align on what Redwood can produce for evidence and how fast.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Got it. Thanks, Lena. Quick context from our side: we'll cover what artifacts live in the Trust Center versus things you get via the API or direct S3 exports, and then walk through a controls matrix map.
[00:28] Marcus Feng: Also, I want to call out we have EU patient data and we need to ensure we can show residency and KMS separation for that tenant.
[00:34] Ava Martinez: Yep, that's a good call out. We'll show both the hosted approach and how Dedicated / Private deployments change the evidence story.
[00:42] Nia O'Connor: One note — sometimes the auto-transcribe swaps "KV cache" with "K V" or "karaoke cache" — so ignore weird bits in the transcript.

[02:05] Sana Rahman: To start, here's where we are: we have SOC 2 Type II readiness internally but are missing some third-party attestation artifacts for services that process PHI. We need a clear list of where Redwood stores logs and how long you retain them by default.
[02:25] Ava Martinez: Understood. By default our hosted API keeps admin/audit logs for 90 days in the console, with export capability to your S3. For Dedicated we can increase retention and we can provide continuous streaming to your SIEM. I know you mentioned PHI — we'll also show the KMS flow and HSM-backed keys for Private deployments.

[04:10] Tom Brewer: Quick Q, what's in the Trust Center vs what requires a support ticket? We can't give auditors broad console access.
[04:17] Samir Patel: Good question. The Trust Center contains redacted SOC 2 report, ISO attestation, system architecture diagrams, and a controls matrix download. Auditor access is via role-based links: you can create a time-limited auditor role that grants read-only access to specific artifacts. No need to give full console access. We'll show the flow.
[04:36] Lena Ortiz: That works — can the auditor get CSV of log events or is it just PDFs and diagrams?
[04:42] Samir Patel: You can export audit logs as either CSV/JSON from the logs API or we can stream them into your S3 in a gzipped JSONL format. The Trust Center provides PDF certs and PDFs of policy docs, plus a CSV controls matrix you can download.

[06:50] Marcus Feng: About encryption: for hosted customers, is Redwood managing the keys? We need to know whether we can bring our own key (BYOK) and route EU keys to EU KMS.
[07:00] Ava Martinez: On hosted, Redwood manages keys by default with envelope encryption. For Dedicated and Private we support BYOK via KMS integrations and can set key tenancy per region. For EU residency we can ensure keys and data stay in the EU region and show KMS key ARNs as evidence.

[09:15] Sana Rahman: For ISO 27001, auditors often want to see evidence of access reviews and RBAC policies. Does Redwood provide a history of role changes and SSO/SAML configuration snapshots?
[09:24] Samir Patel: Yes: we log all admin role changes, SAML configuration changes, and SCIM provisioning events. Those are stored in the audit log and can be exported. We also keep a change history in the Trust Center for SSO metadata snapshots.

[11:05] Tom Brewer: Is the audit log tamper-evident? We need to show chain-of-custody for log exports.
[11:12] Samir Patel: The hosted logs include integrity markers and are stored with append-only policies — we provide a signed manifest on export. For Dedicated/Private, you control the storage and can configure immutable buckets and retention policies.

[13:00] Lena Ortiz: Do you document the control owners mapping? Our auditors will want to see which Redwood control maps to our internal control numbers.
[13:08] Ava Martinez: We have a controls mapping template — we'll share a CSV where columns are Redwood control ID, description, evidence type, sample artifact location, and suggested frequency. Samir will add a sample mapping for the access control group.

[15:30] Samir Patel: (screen-share reference) — here's an example mapping: RWI-AC-01 maps to ISO A.9.2 and SOC CC6. We usually suggest linking to the Trust Center artifact and adding an export path for logs. We'll send the CSV after the call.

[17:40] Marcus Feng: For the EU residency, we need proof that data for EU patients never leaves region. How do you show that?
[17:48] Ava Martinez: We provide a region-scoped export that includes a per-tenant region tag on data and KMS key metadata. For Dedicated, you can pin a model instance to EU GPUs only and we provide deployment logs that show placement. We'll include an example deployment manifest as evidence.

[20:10] Sana Rahman: What about penetration testing and vulnerability scanning reports? Auditors sometimes expect a summary.
[20:18] Nia O'Connor: For hosted customers we publish an annual pen test summary (redacted) in the Trust Center; for Dedicated/Private we can provide the scope and remediation timelines. We usually don't publish raw reports due to third-party NDAs but we can provide an executive summary.

[22:45] Tom Brewer: On SSO, we use Okta. Will Redwood support SCIM provisioning and SAML OIDC snapshots for auditor review?
[22:53] Samir Patel: Yes, Okta provisioning via SCIM is supported. We keep provisioning logs and snapshots and can export SAML metadata in a signed format. We'll include an example metadata snapshot.

[25:12] Lena Ortiz: A practical ask — auditors want to see sample evidence for the last 6 months. Can you provide dated artifacts rather than just a live view?
[25:20] Ava Martinez: Absolutely — we'll provide time-stamped artifacts and sample exports for a rolling 6-month window. For hosted we can generate extracts; for Dedicated we can extract from your configured buckets.

[27:30] Samir Patel: Also note that sometimes customers want a one-off SOC2 bridge letter for a shorter audit window. We can coordinate with our compliance team — that takes a week to produce.

[29:00] Sana Rahman: About data deletion requests — we need to show proof of deletion for certain records. Does Redwood have a deletion audit path?
[29:07] Ava Martinez: Yes, deletion events are logged with who initiated the deletion, time, and the object ID. For Private setups you can also enable purge confirmation receipts that show the object was removed from primary and cold storage.

[31:15] Marcus Feng: One more on logs — do you provide schema or field-level documentation for the audit events so our SIEM team can map them?
[31:22] Samir Patel: We do. There's a logs schema doc in the Trust Center with field descriptions, event types, and example JSON snippets. We'll link that.

[33:40] Lena Ortiz: Ok, last thing — our procurement team is nervous about vendor lock-in and wants exit evidence: how do we show a clean offboarding?
[33:48] Nia O'Connor: We provide an offboarding pack: data export (full dataset), key revocation guidance, and a final audit log dump. For Dedicated you control the final snapshot. For hosted we will provide the final export plus a signed manifest.

[35:55] Tom Brewer: Are there specific RBAC roles for auditors or do we create a custom role?
[36:01] Samir Patel: You can create a pre-defined "auditor_readonly" role which we recommend — it surfaces the Trust Center and artifact downloads but blocks configuration changes. You can also scope to specific projects or tenants.

[38:10] Lena Ortiz: For the controls matrix, can you pre-populate some rows with suggested evidence so our team doesn't have to start from scratch?
[38:17] Ava Martinez: Yes, we'll add sample rows for access control, key management, logging, change management, and incident response. We'll flag which artifacts are in the Trust Center vs API exports.

[40:30] Marcus Feng: A practical integration question — for the SIEM stream, what's the maximum throughput and retention options? We have bursts of 10k events per minute.
[40:38] Samir Patel: We support high-throughput streaming to S3 or Kafka endpoints. For Dedicated, we guarantee throughput to meet your burst profile; we'll need to size the pipeline and maybe allocate burst capacity. Samir: I'll follow up with throughput options in a short note.

[42:50] Sana Rahman: Auditors sometimes ask for encryption attestations. Can Redwood provide KMS key rotation history and key custodianship logs?
[42:58] Samir Patel: Yes — KMS rotation events, key alias changes, and access grants are logged and can be exported. For BYOK we can show proofs of key import and usage logs.

[45:10] Lena Ortiz: Great. Let's do a quick recap and assign next steps.
[45:16] Ava Martinez: Recap: 1) We'll send redacted SOC2 Type II and ISO cert, 2) Samir sends controls mapping template and a sample mapping, 3) we'll give Trust Center read-only auditor role instructions and an example time-limited link, 4) Pioneer to give list of auditors and required evidence types and retention windows.

[45:50] Tom Brewer: Can you also include an example S3 export manifest and signed log manifest?
[45:55] Ava Martinez: Yes — Samir will include both artifacts in the follow-up.

[48:00] Sana Rahman: Any blockers on our side? We'll need to get legal to approve the auditor access and confirm NDA allowances.
[48:07] Ava Martinez: Not from our side. We'll mark access time-limited and provide NDAs if necessary.

[50:20] Nia O'Connor: I'll put links in the follow-up: Trust Center demo link, CSV controls template, and a short IRL runbook for handing evidence to auditors.

[51:30] Lena Ortiz: Timeline check — we need things by Nov 17 to prepare for the auditor pre-work.
[51:36] Ava Martinez: We'll aim to deliver the docs by Nov 12 and mapping by Nov 15 so you can review ahead of Nov 17.

[53:00] Marcus Feng: Thanks everyone, that was helpful. We'll follow up with the list of auditors and confirm the data residency table.
[53:08] Ava Martinez: Thanks — we'll follow up via email and share the drive links.

Meeting end.
